title: MCP walkthrough: a real installation driven in plain language
description: The scale-guinstall MCP calls made during one real installation on 2026-10-06, copied from the session transcripts; the operator's own words are verbatim. Playback pacing is generated.
footer: REAL RUN 2026-10-06 | Real MCP calls, shortened results; generated pacing.
note: Built from the session transcripts of one real run. Silent playback; read the synchronized narration aloud. Starts paused.

scenes.title: A real MCP run, 2026-10-06
lines: Claude Code driving the backend on the installer node
Each ">" line is a real MCP tool call from the session
transcript; indented lines are its result, shortened. Lines
starting USER are the operator's own words, verbatim.
The agent's replies and reasoning are not shown.
scenes.narration: This is the same installation as the command-line and GUI walkthroughs, seen from the MCP side. Every call you see was made by Claude Code against the scale-guinstall MCP server, copied from the session transcript, with the results shortened. Lines marked USER are the operator's own words, verbatim. The agent's replies and reasoning are not shown, and the playback pacing is generated.

scenes.title: 1. Is the environment ready?
scenes.narration: The operator said the new environment, tunnel and server were up. The agent checked: the backend answers ping, the toolkit is version 6.0.1.1, ansible-core 2.14.18 is compatible, the installer's address is 10.249.129.192, and no operation is running.

scenes.title: 2. Look at the disks
scenes.narration: Next the agent listed the block devices on both storage servers. Each has ten devices and three free 100 gigabyte disks: vdd, vde and vdf. Those become the NSDs.

scenes.title: 3. Start the installation service
scenes.narration: Setup ran first as a dry run, which only validates and prints the command, and then for real. Operations return as soon as they start, so the agent polls check_operation; setup finished in two and a half seconds.

scenes.title: 4. Define the seven nodes
scenes.narration: One call defines all seven nodes and their roles; the backend turns it into a delete and an add per node. While it runs, the agent polls spectrumscale_running about every two seconds, because the toolkit allows only one command at a time. It finished in thirty-four seconds.

scenes.title: 5. Read the nodes back
scenes.narration: Reading the node list back shows the toolkit expanded each short name to its full host name and kept the roles exactly as requested.

scenes.title: 6. Define the storage
scenes.narration: One call adds all six NSDs: the first two disks on each server for data and metadata, the third for data only in a pool named data, with failure groups one and two. The agent then listed them back, six in all.

scenes.title: 7. Call home and cluster settings
scenes.narration: Call home is disabled, and the cluster settings set the ephemeral port range to 60000 through 61000. The results are the commands the backend ran.

scenes.title: 8. The protocols were applied in the GUI
lines: The NFS, SMB and S3 settings were applied from the GUI's
Apply Protocols panel, not through MCP in this run.
See slide 16 of the GUI walkthrough for that step.
scenes.narration: One step in this run did not go through MCP. The protocols were configured and enabled from the GUI's Apply Protocols panel, while the screenshots for the GUI walkthrough were being taken.

scenes.title: 9. Precheck and install
scenes.narration: The install precheck ran, and then the operator said go ahead with install. The install takes about twenty-five minutes, so the agent checked in only now and then. When it asked for the result, the tool returned an error: the output was over a hundred and twenty thousand characters, too big for one result. The output had been saved to a file, which the agent read from there. That is a limit of the tool, not a failure of the install.

scenes.title: 10. Check the install
scenes.narration: The install postcheck ran next. Its result is in the command-line walkthrough, which shows every phase with its real timing.

scenes.title: 11. A new session picks up
scenes.narration: The session was then cleared, and a new one started from a short hand-off note the operator pasted. Before doing anything, the agent checked that the backend still answered and that nothing was running. The operator's reply to the plan was go for it.

scenes.title: 12. A wrong argument, caught by a dry run
scenes.narration: The first deploy precheck call was a dry run, and it failed: the toolkit argument must be the spectrumscale file, not the folder that holds it. Because it was a dry run, nothing was executed, and the corrected call validated. This is a real mistake, left in.

scenes.title: 13. Precheck, deploy and postcheck
scenes.narration: The deploy precheck took about two and a half minutes. The deploy ran for seventeen and a half minutes while the agent waited with SSH checks from the operator's Mac. Asking for its result hit the same size limit as the install, so the output was read from the saved file. The postcheck then finished in under ten seconds.

scenes.title: 14. Read it back, then record
lines: The verification commands were then recorded live.
See the verification recording in the CLI walkthrough.
scenes.narration: A last read of the node list shows seven nodes with S3, SMB and NFS enabled. The operator then asked to record, and the build. The verification commands were recorded live from the operator's Mac, and the walkthroughs were rebuilt from the real data.
